standard.title: Alphabet and language features construct meaning
standard.description: recognise that the Roman alphabet and features of language are used to construct meaning in the target language
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have noticed basic grammatical patterns with support (AC9LSF02). They are developing early literacy in English using the Roman alphabet. They have no prior systematic knowledge of target language grammatical structures.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise how the alphabet and key grammatical features — including word class markers, agreement patterns, verb forms and basic sentence structure — are used to construct meaning in the target language.

nodes.label: Grammatical markers and word class features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise how grammatical markers in the target language signal word class, agreement and relationships between words — and apply these in familiar word groups.
nodes.minimum_width: Correctly use grammatical markers (e.g. articles, agreement markers) with at least four familiar words; produce at least two word groups showing correct agreement.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and apply grammatical agreement patterns across familiar vocabulary; observe word order patterns; notice how endings and markers signal relationships between words; use possessive forms; produce simple descriptive word groups with correct agreement.
wider: Sort a set of unfamiliar target language words into grammatical categories using patterns and context clues — explain the rule applied
Identify every grammatical marker in a short familiar text and describe what each one signals
nodes.hinge_reason: Grammatical agreement and word class markers are the foundational system governing noun-phrase and sentence production in the target language. Students who do not internalise these patterns produce systematic errors that cascade throughout all sentence production at every subsequent band.

response_modes.reason: Grammatical agreement requires high-frequency practice across a wide range of vocabulary before it becomes automatic. Students need to encounter and produce marked forms in varied contexts — not only in drills but in real text creation and comprehension.

success_criteria: Uses correct grammatical markers with at least four familiar words
Produces at least two word groups with correct agreement patterns

nodes.label: Verb forms and affirmative/negative statements
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise basic verb forms in the target language and produce simple affirmative and negative statements.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least two affirmative statements and one negative statement using correct basic verb forms.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and use basic verb forms; produce simple affirmative and negative statements; notice how subject information is encoded in verb forms; use number expressions for age, time and dates; use possessive forms in familiar expressions.
wider: Produce statements using at least three different verbs — demonstrating a growing verb repertoire beyond the most frequent
Find the same verb used with different subjects in a familiar text — describe the pattern that signals each person

response_modes.reason: Verb form recognition and basic statement production develops through accumulating examples across varied verbs and sentence contexts before inflection patterns become recognisable.

success_criteria: Produces at least two affirmative statements and one negative statement using correct basic verb forms
Uses at least one verb in a recognisable inflected form

nodes.label: Sentence-level composition and target language conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce connected sentences in the target language and identify key written conventions that differ from English.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least two connected sentences; identify at least one written convention of the target language that differs from English.
nodes.typical_width: Produce connected sentences using connectors to link ideas; identify distinctive punctuation, capitalisation or orthographic conventions of the target language; notice how target language written conventions differ from English; produce simple texts with two or more connected statements.
wider: Produce three or four connected sentences about a topic — demonstrating early sentence-level composition that creates a coherent mini-text
Compare the written conventions of a target language and English sentence — identify every difference and explain each

response_modes.reason: Sentence-level composition develops through encountering and producing varied sentence types in real text contexts. Varied production contexts build the compositional habit beyond isolated drills.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Early sentence composition — producing connected statements rather than isolated phrases — is the production foundation for all text creation in subsequent bands.
success_criteria: Produces at least two connected sentences that form a coherent mini-text
Identifies at least one target language written convention that differs from English and explains the difference
